speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ukraine is a large country with a multilingual and multi-religious population of approximately 44 million people.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It has a long history, with complex relations with Russia and other states in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ukraine became independent in 1991, with the collapse of the Soviet Union.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Since then, the Ukraine has faced considerable domestic political turmoil, exacerbated by the separatist movements and tensions with Russia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Conflicts on the ground in Donbas have continued for the past eight years, with episodic limited ceasefires.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And beginning in spring 2021, Russia massed over 100,000 troops at its borders with Ukraine.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In January 2022, cyberattacks were launched against the Ukrainian government websites.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On 21 February 2022, Russia recognised two breakaway Ukrainian regions and announced that Russian troops would start performing what it called "peacekeeping operations".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On 24 February 2022, Russia announced the start of a "special military operation" in Ukraine.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This was followed shortly by air, land and sea attacks on multiple targets across the whole of Ukraine.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Russian ground forces, including armoured formations, rapidly entered Ukraine from the north, the south and the east, and have reached the capital Kyiv.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: While Ukraine is far away from us, we are following the crisis with grave concern.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Its economic effects can already be felt here, for example, in rising electricity and petrol prices.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Minister Gan Kim Yong will address the economic issues later today.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But these are not the principal reason the situation in Ukraine is important to us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The events in Ukraine go to the heart of the fundamental norms of international law and the UN Charter that prohibit the use of force and acts of aggression against another sovereign state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ukraine is much smaller than Russia, but it is much bigger than Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: A world order based on "might is right", or where "the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must", such a world order would be profoundly inimical to the security and survival of small states.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We cannot accept one country attacking another without justification, arguing that its independence was the result of "historical errors and crazy decisions".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Such a rationale would go against the internationally recognised legitimacy and territorial integrity of many countries, including Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That is why we are a staunch supporter of international law, and the principles enshrined in the UN Charter.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The sovereignty, political independence and the territorial integrity of all countries, big and small, must be respected.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is heartbreaking to see the heavy casualties and loss of many innocent lives, resulting from this unjustified attack and act of war.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We strongly urge Russia to cease this offensive military action immediately and to work for a peaceful settlement in accordance with the UN Charter and international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also call for safe and unhindered access for humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and all those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Singapore Red Cross has pledged a contribution of US$100,000 to support communities affected by the current crisis, in cooperation with the Ukrainian Red Cross Society and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This will provide essential relief supplies, such as hygiene kits, family kits and household kits for the vulnerable who have been displaced by the conflict.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In addition, the Singapore Red Cross has launched a public fundraising appeal to support the impending massive humanitarian operations that will be needed.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Government will also contribute US$100,000 to this humanitarian operation through the Singapore Red Cross.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: First, whilst international law and diplomatic principles are essential, they are not sufficient.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Budapest Memorandum was supposed to guarantee Ukraine's security by three nuclear powers – Russia, the US and the UK.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But agreements are only meaningful if the parties respect them and if they can be enforced.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The invasion of Ukraine demonstrates how quickly a vulnerable country can be overrun, especially when confronting a larger and more powerful opponent.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is the acute reality for all small countries and Singapore is no exception.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014 and Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990 are stark reminders of this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: You cannot depend on others to protect your country.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The capability of the SAF must be undergirded by Singaporeans' resolve – the iron determination of our people to fight and die, if need be, to defend what is ours and our way of life.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Without such capability and resolve, no amount of diplomacy can save a country.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Second, it is all too easy for a small country to be caught up in the geopolitical games of big powers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Small countries must avoid becoming sacrificial pawns, vassal states or "cat's paws" to be used by one side against the other.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In a speech delivered in 1973, former Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew had shared his agreement with Julius Nyerere, the then-President of Tanzania, who had said, "When elephants fight, the grass suffers".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is why we work hard to maintain good relations with all our neighbours and with the big powers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When situations arise, our assessments and actions are based on clearly enunciated and consistently held principles that are in our own long-term national interests.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Consequently, we conduct our foreign policy in a coherent and consistent manner.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also become reliable partners for those who operate on the same principles.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However, there will occasions when we will have to take a stand, even if it is contrary to one or more powers on the basis of principles – as we are doing now.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Third, as a young nation, it is vital for us to maintain domestic unity and cohesion, bearing in mind how easily internal divisions can be exploited by adversaries, especially in this Internet age and the advent of hybrid warfare.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Dividing and weakening an opponent internally, overtly and covertly, has become a standard complement to conventional warfare.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Therefore, our domestic politics must stop at our shores.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I thank all Members of Parliament for adhering to this precept.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I would share that I have also shared this point with the Leader of the Opposition, Mr Pritam Singh.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Fourth, safeguarding one's sovereignty and national interests often requires some sacrifice and pain.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Ukrainians are paying the ultimate price for freedom with their lives and livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The rest of the international community that is taking a stand against naked aggression through sanctions will also have to bear some pain and pay a price.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans too must understand that standing up for our national interests may come with some cost.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must be prepared to deal with the consequences, to bear the pain, to help one another and to stand up together.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We continue to value our good relations with Russia and the Russian people.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However, we cannot accept such violations of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of another sovereign country.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to work with our ASEAN and international partners to take a strong stance against the invasion of Ukraine, and to end further violence and bloodshed, and to de-escalate tensions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also participate actively at the United Nations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Three days ago, a draft resolution was presented at the UN Security Council (UNSC) to condemn Russia's aggression against Ukraine.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore was one of 82 co-sponsors of this Security Council resolution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As expected, Russia, as a Permanent Member of the Security Council, vetoed that resolution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, the resolution was not passed even though 11 of the 15 Security Council members voted in support and the remaining three members – China, India and the UAE – abstained.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The UN General Assembly (UNGA) will be debating a similar resolution later today.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: General Assembly resolutions are not subject to a veto, but neither are they binding.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However, as a responsible member of the international community, Singapore will comply with the spirit and the letter of the UN General Assembly's decision.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The specific measures are being worked out and will be announced shortly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I note that Dr Lim Wee Kiak1 and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim2 have filed Parliamentary Questions on the current situation in Ukraine, especially on the steps taken by MFA to help Singaporeans in Ukraine.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I would be happy to address their concerns in a clarification after this and if the concerns are sufficiently addressed, they can consider withdrawing the subsequent Parliamentray Questions and save time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We advised Singaporeans in Ukraine to leave as soon as possible via commercial means while it was still possible to do so at that point in time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans in Ukraine were also urged to e-register with MFA, so that we could render consular assistance to them.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the meantime, Singaporeans who are in Ukraine are advised to seek shelter in place, be vigilant and to heed the advice from the authorities.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Those who have not yet e-registered with MFA should do so immediately.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Given that Singapore has cordial relations with the US, Europe, Ukraine and Russia, to what extent have the recent events put our efforts out of balance?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And how can we maintain our interest vis-à-vis all the parties?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We do have excellent relations with the US, with the EU, with Russia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And of course, we have diplomatic relations with Ukraine as well.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I explained just now that Singapore's foreign policy is consistent, is coherent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I can tell you now, from experience, from the past six to seven years with the privilege of representing Singapore on stage, is that big powers and our neighbours and middle powers have also gotten used to the fact that it is not personal, it is professional, it is principled.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We take a position based on these principles which we believe to be essential for our long-term national interest.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I can also tell you, although there is no time to go through all the details now, that even in my tenure over the past six or seven years, I have had to say no, on occasion, to every single superpower.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But it has not stopped us from being able to sit at the table, look at each other's eyes, shake hands, explain where we defer, why we defer and at the same time, to pursue areas of cooperation where our interests align and where our principles are shared.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, this is not new, this is not a new posture.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This in fact, is a posture that we have adopted for every single year since we have been independent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second question: are the events in far away Ukraine possibly a model and inspiration or an invitation for similar incursions elsewhere?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I will not speculate where other clashes will erupt around the world except to tell you – and I am sure you are also aware as a former diplomat yourself – that we are not short of hotspots in the world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, I will bring us back to this fundamental point that we talked about – deterrence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For deterrence to work, first, we ourselves must have the capability to defend ourselves.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And there is one additional dimension: that your partner or your protagonist on the other side must also have arrived at that same conclusion – that you have both the capability and resolve to defend.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is how you secure peace in a dangerous world.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The first is the United Nations has always been an important institution, at least for setting the benchmark against aggression.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But would this send a message that it will be difficult to restrain big powers from engaging in acts of aggression and is there more the world community can do in this respect?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I know Singapore is just a small voice in that, but is there more that the world community can do in this engagement?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The second is, in relation to specific measures that Singapore may take, this will be elaborated on later, but I think it will be important for whatever we do in this message to send the clear signal that we stand against these acts of aggression and the UN Charter must be upheld.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is always difficult to restrain big powers or emerging big powers, who will always give precedence to their national interests defined on their terms.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, let us have no illusions about this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For what it is worth, having international law, having avenues of peaceful resolution on disputes, having the United Nations with its Charter, having instruments like the Security Council and the General Assembly, capable of establishing norms, capable, sometimes – assuming there is no veto – of arriving at Security Council resolutions, is valuable.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But, my point is that you cannot rely on that alone.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Every country, big or small, has to have the capability and the resolve to defend itself, then to make common cause on the basis of principle with other like-minded countries.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And for what it is worth, try to establish norms of state behaviour.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But human history is replete with conflicts, conflicts which when you look back in hindsight make no sense, brought far more harm than any objective that was sought at the beginning, or simply miscalculations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, again, I am making the point that for what it is worth, we uphold principles, we do not take sides.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And that is the formula to preserve our future security and prosperity.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am thankful for the answers to my Parliamentary Question as well, wherein I asked about assistance to fellow Singaporeans who are embroiled in that conflict.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: First is, I think both the virus and violence are taking a toll on the people in the Ukrainian region.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, it is going to be a great humanitarian crisis and the refugee situation in Eastern Europe will also be unprecedented.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What can ASEAN and Singapore do to alleviate the situation over there, particularly, given that COVID-19 is still raging amongst us and there would be some need to render assistance in that regard?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But at the same time, we still need to know the lay of the land and navigate our way through.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, what are the implications in terms of international order, particularly for Singapore and smaller states, given this particular crisis that is unravelling before us?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we will work through the Ukrainian Red Cross, the International Society of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I hope there will be a humanitarian impulse from ASEAN as well.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Specifically, for the citizens of ASEAN who may be stranded.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I just want to share one little anecdote which also illustrates the point.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I said that three Singaporeans managed to cross the border in a perilous time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I can say that at least one did so in a convoy together with Malaysian citizens who were crossing the border into Poland.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I thank my counterpart in Malaysia for that.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Similarly, on the ground, I am sure we will continue to work with each other, look out for citizens of ASEAN and where possible, "tumpang", "gotong royong" and help one another.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think these are teachable moments, good opportunities for ASEAN to demonstrate value and solidarity with each other where it matters.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second question on what are the implications of this crisis?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First off, we already feel the economic impact and Minister Gan will be dealing with this later today.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I said, standing up for principle is not cost-free.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we also have to be prepared for that.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But, if the world continues to watch with folded arms, we are headed into a much more dangerous world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: After the end of the Second World War in 1945 and the establishment of the European Union, I think many people thought war on the European Continent was unthinkable.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Clearly, that rosy view is wrong, and you are watching, again, war on European soil in an advanced beautiful capital today.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: One is on Ukrainians who are currently in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Are we going to help them to extend, while their country is currently in crisis now?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Does the Minister have the numbers as to how many Ukrainians are currently in Singapore, for whatever reasons?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Number two, what is the proper channel for us to channel resources to help now?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The Minister mentioned about Red Cross is one resource.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Will the Government have a concerted effort to have fundraising efforts from the public to help the Ukrainian, rather to have multiple websites and we do not know which is the one that is approved and authorised?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Also, currently, the Ukrainian President is calling for the foreign legion to help the country, for fighters to come in.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If any Singaporeans were to volunteer to become a fighter to go to Ukraine, will the Government object or will the Government stop them?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not have the figures on Ukrainians who are currently in Singapore and the passes that they are on.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Nevertheless, we will look at it case-by-case, depending on the merits of the particular situation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On channels, my advice would be to support the Singapore Red Cross.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think that is clear, reputable and safe.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies were created precisely to have a role in such conflict situations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I would encourage people who are minded to provide humanitarian assistance to work through the Red Cross.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On the third question about the foreign legion, again, I will have to come back to principle.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our long-standing rules and regulatory system must continue to apply.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore Citizens, your duty is to Singapore, to fight and die if need be, to defend our national interests and to take a long-term view of what our national interests are.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I just have one clarification for the Minister for Foreign Affairs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Will the Government be exploring the initiation of a common position on this very grave issue with the other ASEAN member states?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Is that something that will be looked at, in spite of the challenges in doing so, which obviously do exist and that is very clear?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I have said, we recently – in fact, I think just a day ago – issued an ASEAN common statement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I will be frank and tell you that the 10 of us will have a variety of views, but I am glad that we were able to issue a consensus statement that reaffirmed mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I also hope that there will be cooperation on humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and, as I said earlier, also cooperation on helping each other's citizens emerge safely from a conflict situation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Second clarification is that, would the Minister be able to clarify or explain what MFA thinks about Russia's statement that they will be "putting nuclear forces on high alert".

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Would Singaporeans who are staying in NATO countries be considered safe or would there be advice that they were to evacuate from those countries as well?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: China abstained at the vote on the resolution that was presented to the United Nations Security Council.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second point is that China has expressed some solidarity, at least more so in recent times, and some sympathy for Russian concerns.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My third observation is that I believe China does hold firmly to the principle of independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Beyond that, I do not wish to speculate but I do want to assure the Member that we have been, as always, in constant contact with my Chinese counterpart.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, President Halimah and I were in Beijing, I think just three weeks ago.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am not even sure that the Olympic truce has expired yet and I will not be able to reveal details.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we, certainly, had an opportunity to listen to the leadership of China's views on unfolding events.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But that was three weeks ago, before the hot conflict emerged.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not want to speculate into the Member's second question about the impact of elevation of the nuclear alert.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And every time a nuclear power gets into a hot war, we need to be very, very concerned.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Beyond that, I do not wish to speculate except, again, to express our hope that there is so much more to lose from letting the situation get out of control.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, our hope is that restraint will apply, there will be an immediate cessation of hostilities and violence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I believe there had been some arrangements for negotiations to occur between Ukraine and Russia at the border with Belarus, perhaps today or maybe even as we speak.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I hope those negotiations will bear some fruit.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Member's point is that this is a dangerous time and we all need to be concerned.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Speaker, I thank the Minister for clarifying Singapore's stand.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Beyond declaring our principles, I would like to ask if the Government would review the ongoing initiatives and projects, whether economic, defence or cultural, with the Russian government and any of the government-linked organisations, especially for those based in Singapore, and decide after the review, what action it will take that will support the principles that the Minister had just articulated?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And as I have said, we are working through the details.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I do not want to run ahead and I do not want to engage in speculation but to just make the point that we have no quarrel with the Russian people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think the Member was indirectly alluding to the project that we have on the Russian Orthodox Church building and I would imagine that this is a project which, in my own view, should continue because this goes beyond the politics and the conflict which is going on right now.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.
